arxiv-1905-09648.title: Three-dimensional charge transport mapping by two-photon absorption edge transient-current technique in synthetic single-crystalline diamond
arxiv-1905-09648.creator: C. Dorfer, D. Hits, L. Kasmi, G. Kramberger, M. Lucchini, M. Mikuž, R. Wallny
arxiv-1905-09648.description: Abstract We demonstrate the application of two-photon absorption transient current technique to wide bandgap semiconductors. We utilize it to probe charge transport properties of single-crystal Chemical Vapor Deposition (scCVD) diamond. The charge carriers, inside the scCVD diamond sample, are excited by a femtosecond laser through simultaneous absorption of two photons.

arxiv-2012-08041.title: NUTA: Non-uniform Temporal Aggregation for Action Recognition
arxiv-2012-08041.creator: Xinyu Li, Chunhui Liu, Bing Shuai, Yi Zhu, Hao Chen, Joseph Tighe Amazon Web Services {xxnl, chunhliu, bshuai, yzaws, hxen, tighej}@amazon.com
arxiv-2012-08041.description: Abstract In the world of action recognition research, one primary focus has been on how to construct and train networks to model the spatial-temporal volume of an input video. These methods typically uniformly sample a segment of an input clip (along the temporal dimension).

arxiv-2103-00891.title: Using contrastive learning to improve the performance of steganalysis schemes Conference: 9th ACM Workshop on Information Hiding and Multimedia Security; June 21–25, 2021; IH&MMSEC Brussels, Belgium
arxiv-2103-00891.creator: Yanzhen Ren, Yiwen Liu, Lina Wang
arxiv-2103-00891.description: Abstract . To improve the detection accuracy and generalization of steganalysis, this paper proposes the Steganalysis Contrastive Framework (SCF) based on contrastive learning. The SCF improves the feature representation of steganalysis by maximizing the distance between features of samples of different categories and minimizing the distance between features of samples of the same category.

arxiv-2206-06895.title: The cortical V1 transform as a heterogeneous Poisson problem
arxiv-2206-06895.creator: A.Sarti, M.Galeotti, G.Citti
arxiv-2206-06895.description: Abstract Receptive profiles of the primary visual cortex (V1) cortical cells are very heterogeneous and act by differentiating the stimulus image as operators changing from point to point. In this paper we aim to show that the distribution of cells in V1, although not complete to reconstruct the original image, is sufficient to reconstruct the perceived image with subjective constancy.

arxiv-2303-09227.title: MROS: A framework for robot self-adaptation
arxiv-2303-09227.creator: Gustavo Rezende Silva, Darko Bozhinoski, Mario Garzon Oviedo, Mariano Ramírez Montero, Nadia Hammoudeh Garcia, Harshavardhan Deshpande, Andrzej Wasowski, Carlos Hernandez Corbato
arxiv-2303-09227.description: Abstract . Self-adaptation can be used in robotics to increase system robustness and reliability. This work describes the Metacontrol method for self-adaptation in robotics. Particularly, it details how the MROS (Metacontrol for ROS Systems) framework implements and packages Metacontrol, and it demonstrate how MROS can be applied in a navigation scenario where a mobile robot navigates in a factory floor.

arxiv-2304-06399.title: Choreographic Programming of Isolated Transactions
arxiv-2304-06399.creator: Ton Smeele, Sung-Shik Jongmans
arxiv-2304-06399.description: Abstract Implementing distributed systems is hard; choreographic programming aims to make it easier. In this paper, we present the design of a new choreographic programming language that supports isolated transactions among overlapping sets of processes. The first idea is to track for every variable which processes are permitted to use it.

arxiv-2310-13677.title: Intriguing Plasma Composition Pattern in a Solar Active Region: a Result of Non-Resonant Alfvén Waves? SolarSoftWare ( Freeland & Handy 1998 ) , EISPAC ( Weberg et al. 2023 )
arxiv-2310-13677.creator: Teodora Mihailescu, David H. Brooks, J. Martin Laming, Deborah Baker, Lucie M. Green, Alexander W. James, David M. Long, Lidia van Driel-Gesztelyi, Marco Stangalini
arxiv-2310-13677.description: Abstract The plasma composition of the solar corona is different from that of the solar photosphere. Elements that have a low first ionisation potential (FIP) are preferentially transported to the corona and, therefore, show enhanced abundances in the corona compared to the photosphere. The level of enhancement is measured using the FIP bias parameter.

arxiv-2411-19149.title: Counting Stacked Objects
arxiv-2411-19149.creator: Corentin Dumery, Noa Etté, Aoxiang Fan, Ren Li, Jingyi Xu, Hieu Le, Pascal Fua
arxiv-2411-19149.description: Abstract Visual object counting is a fundamental computer vision task underpinning numerous real-world applications, from cell counting in biomedicine to traffic and wildlife monitoring. However, existing methods struggle to handle the challenge of stacked 3D objects in which most objects are hidden by those above them.

arxiv-2412-16370.title: Faster Positional-Population Counts for AVX2, AVX-512, and ASIMD

arxiv-2412-16370.description: Abstract The positional population count operation pospopcnt counts for an array of w w -bit words how often each of the w w bits was set. Various applications in bioinformatics, database engineering, and digital processing exist. Building on earlier work by Klarqvist et al.

arxiv-2508-15357.title: KG-EDAS: A Meta-Metric Framework for Evaluating Knowledge Graph Completion Models
arxiv-2508-15357.creator: Haji Gul, Abul Ghani Naim, Ajaz Ahmad Bhat
arxiv-2508-15357.description: Abstract Knowledge Graphs (KGs) enable applications in various domains such as semantic search, recommendation systems, and natural language processing. KGs are often incomplete, missing entities and relations, an issue addressed by Knowledge Graph Completion (KGC) methods that predict missing elements. arxiv-2509-21478.title: Modeling discrete lattice data using the Potts and tapered Potts models
arxiv-2509-21478.creator: Maria Paula Duenas-Herrera
arxiv-2509-21478.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Maria Paula Duenas-Herrera. The Ising and Potts models, among the most important models in statistical physics, have been used for modeling binary and multinomial data on lattices in a wide variety of disciplines such as psychology, image analysis, biology, and forestry.

arxiv-2511-20320.title: Revisiting lepton flavor violation: τ \tau and meson decays
arxiv-2511-20320.creator: Kevin A. Urquía-Calderón, and Oleg Ruchayskiy
arxiv-2511-20320.description: Abstract The minimal type-I seesaw model provides a simple explanation of neutrino flavor oscillations and induces charged lepton flavor violation (cLFV). Despite extensive previous studies, semileptonic cLFV channels remain underexplored. Using updated form factors, decay constants, and oscillation data, we revisit τ \tau and meson decay channels, performing a systematic comparison across the seesaw parameter space.

arxiv-2602-20604.title: Correlator-Level Verification of Mass and Current Maps in Abelian Chern–Simons Dualities
arxiv-2602-20604.description: Abstract We construct an explicit local operator realization that reproduces Dirac fermion correlation functions in three spacetime dimensions within an Abelian Chern–Simons framework and use it to examine the conjectured operator and deformation maps of fermion–boson duality directly at the level of correlation functions.

pmc-10624909.title: The inverse association between DNA gaps and HbA1c levels in type 2 diabetes mellitus
pmc-10624909.creator: Jirapan Thongsroy, Apiwat Mutirangura
pmc-10624909.description: Naturally occurring DNA gaps have been observed in eukaryotic DNA, including DNA in nondividing cells. These DNA gaps are found less frequently in chronologically aging yeast, chemically induced senescence cells, naturally aged rats, d-galactose-induced aging model rats, and older people. These gaps function to protect DNA from damage, so we named them youth-associated genomic stabilization DNA gaps (youth-DNA-gaps).

pmc-10718574.description: Objectives: This study aims to identify various risk factors for acute peripancreatic fluid collections (APFCs) in patients presenting with acute pancreatitis (AP).Methods: A blinded retrospective case-control study was conducted at a tertiary care hospital in Riyadh. Data from 327 patients who presented with AP between January 2008 and 2021 were analyzed.

pmc-10742829.title: Quality Characteristics of Raspberry Fruits from Dormancy Plants and Their Feasibility as Food Ingredients
pmc-10742829.creator: Sílvia Petronilho, Manuel A Coimbra, Cláudia P Passos, Gianluca Nardone, Rosaria Viscecchia, Francesco Bimbo
pmc-10742829.description: The raspberry (Rubus idaeus L.) is a soft red fruit consumed worldwide due to its bitter-sweet taste and phenolics-associated health benefits. During plant dormancy, raspberry fruits are discarded. However, this work hypothesised that these fruits have the chemical quality to be valorised, which would mitigate their waste if adequately stabilised. This can be achieved by drying.

pmc-11475971.title: Recommended Physiotherapy Modalities for Oncology Patients with Palliative Needs and Its Influence on Patient-Reported Outcome Measures: A Systematic Review
pmc-11475971.creator: Luna Gauchez, Shannon Lauryn L. Boyle, Shinfu Selena Eekman, Sarah Harnie, Lore Decoster, Filip Van Ginderdeuren, Len De Nys, Nele Adriaenssens
pmc-11475971.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Simple SummaryThis review explores the role of physiotherapy in early and traditional palliative care (PC) for cancer patients, focusing on its effects on patient-reported outcomes (PROMs) such as fatigue, pain, and quality of life (QoL). The findings suggest that certain physiotherapy interventions, like cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) and massage, can improve these outcomes, while others show limited or no significant benefits.

pmc-11508932.title: Non-Feeding Transmission Modes of the Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus by the Whitefly Bemisia tabaci Do Not Contribute to Reoccurring Leaf Curl Outbreaks in Tomato
pmc-11508932.creator: Wendy G. Marchant, Judith K. Brown, Saurabh Gautam, Saptarshi Ghosh, Alvin M. Simmons, Rajagopalbabu Srinivasan
pmc-11508932.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Simple SummaryTomato yellow leaf curl virus (TYLCV) poses a serious constraint to tomato production in the Southeastern United States. Since its introduction, it has become endemic in states such as Georgia and Florida despite tomato-free periods. This study examined whether the endemic status of TYLCV is aided by the Bemisia tabaci B cryptic species’ vertical and/or horizontal non-feeding modes of TYLCV (the Georgia variant of the Israel strain) transmission. The potential for ‘non-feeding’ transmission modes has been examined previously, with inconsistent results.

pmc-12584045.title: Managing treatment-resistant schizophrenia following clozapine cessation: a case report of xanomeline–trospium and olanzapine combination therapy
pmc-12584045.creator: Nils Sumegi Went, Juan D. Alonso, Rosemarie R. Rigunay, Jason Hershberger, Xiao Xiong You
pmc-12584045.description: BackgroundClozapine is the gold standard for treatment-resistant schizophrenia (TRS) but is limited by rare, serious adverse events. Venous thromboembolism (VTE) and pulmonary embolism (PE) represent particularly challenging complications given their multifactorial pathophysiology, unpredictable recurrence risk, and lack of clear guidance on rechallenge.

uslaw-usc-t10-s8721.title: 10 U.S.C. § 8721 — Jurisdiction and control
uslaw-usc-t10-s8721.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t10-s8721.description: United States Code, Title 10 (Armed Forces); Part IV (General Administration); Chapter 869 (Naval Petroleum Reserves). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) The Secretary shall take possession of all properties inside the naval petroleum reserves that are or may become subject to the control of and use by the United States for national defense purposes, except as otherwise provided in this chapter.
